critical.endpoint: POST /api/admin/gamemaker/test-delayed-job (and any job_engine.submit call without idem_key)
critical.issue: job_engine.submit() creates jobs with idem_key=None. MongoDB collection gm_jobs has a *sparse unique* index on idem_key. Sparse only skips indexing when the FIELD IS MISSING, not when its value is explicitly None. Since submit() always sets idem_key (to None if not provided), the second insert throws DuplicateKeyError, submit()'s except-block then does find_one({'idem_key': None}) and returns the FIRST completed job forever. Repro: 3 consecutive POSTs to /api/admin/gamemaker/test-delayed-job returned identical job_id=b8f66ca5f8404e13ad932588aed980d6; DB shows only 1 gm_test_delay doc across many API hits (verified via backend logs and db.gm_jobs.count_documents). This silently breaks the job engine for every kind that doesn't pass idem_key. Fix: either (a) don't set the idem_key field when None (use $unset / omit from dict), or (b) in submit() replay-guard only when idem_key is truthy: `if idem_key: ex = find_one({'idem_key': idem_key})` (already done) AND in the except handler also `if idem_key and (ex := find_one(...))`.

action_items: CRITICAL: Fix job_engine.submit() idem_key=None duplicate-key trap. Either omit the field entirely when idem_key is falsy (so the sparse index actually skips it) or only look up existing job in the except block when idem_key is truthy. Right now every job kind that doesn't pass idem_key (test-delayed-job, non-idempotent create paths, etc.) will replay the very first stored job forever. This is why the review's own smoke test 'saw' a 65s completed job — every subsequent submit returns the same completed doc, not a new one.
Optional: register handlers for ORAi NAV_SECTIONS ids ['ai-command','private-access','ai-usage'] or mark them soon:true to remove console error at /admin/orai load.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/services/job_engine.py submit(): sparse unique index on idem_key + always-set idem_key=None is a classic Mongo footgun. Also, the except-Exception fallback swallows *any* insert failure (not just duplicate key), so unrelated errors could silently return a stale job.
Consider changing gm_jobs index from sparse to partial: {partialFilterExpression: {idem_key: {$type: 'string'}}} which correctly ignores null.
/admin/orai still fires NAV_SECTIONS validation error at page load (visible in console). Suggests some navigation entries were added without router bindings.

rca of the issue: Bug: /api/admin/gamemaker/test-delayed-job returns the same job_id on every call. RCA: In backend/services/job_engine.py:submit(), the job doc is built with idem_key set to whatever was passed (None if omitted). db.gm_jobs has index {idem_key:1, unique:true, sparse:true}. Sparse only excludes documents where the field is entirely missing — not where field==null. So on the first submit without idem_key the doc inserts fine; on the second, insert throws DuplicateKeyError (E11000 duplicate key idem_key: null). The bare `except Exception` block then does find_one({'idem_key': None}) and returns the first stored no-idem-key job. All subsequent same-kind submits without idem_key return that same job. Verified by (a) 3× POSTs returning identical job_id, (b) db.gm_jobs.count_documents({kind:'gm_test_delay'})==1 despite ~7 API hits in logs, (c) index_information showing sparse unique idem_key_1. Mitigation: change job doc build to only include idem_key when truthy, OR change the index to a partial index filtering on {idem_key:{$type:'string'}}. Also tighten the except handler to (i) only fall back when idem_key is truthy and (ii) narrow to DuplicateKeyError.
